note: Same prospect and same assessment as his two calls on 11 June, with both the successful and the income criteria now much better evidenced on this call. Successful is confirmed twice over — "I'm a financial advisor" and "I own a company. I run a company. I have several employees" — which is squarely the profile the ICP quote describes. Income, however, has moved from a timing problem to a genuine one: "just three months ago, I literally had a half a million dollars just sitting in the bank... All that money is gone. It all went to save my marriage and my house", plus another $27,000 added to the remodel that day and arguments at home over $500. He earns well and has nothing available, and he refused a $1,200 one-month entry as readily as the $6,000. good_to_great and not_deconditioned both fail on the same underlying facts as before: 215 lb at 6'1" with self-reported 28-30% body fat, no training routine, and a frozen elbow and torn ankle ligaments that he himself thinks may make training premature. What this call adds to the ICP picture is a criterion the stated definition does not contain and probably should: evidence of fit for the prospect's age cohort. He asked repeatedly for outcomes from men over 50 and could not be given any, and that — not price — is what he was actually stuck on.
